thread.title: Apple HomePod loses to Google, Sonos in sound tests, says Consumer Reports - MarketWatch

author: Emily Bary
title: Apple HomePod loses to Google, Sonos in sound tests, says Consumer Reports - MarketWatch
text:
Sound quality was the biggest positive for reviewers in judging the Apple Inc. HomePod last week, but the folks at Consumer Reports think that the device’s audio doesn’t quite stack up.
The publication deemed the HomePod’s audio quality strong in a review published Friday , but it fell short of the sound performance of the Sonos One and Alphabet Inc.’s GOOGL, +0.89% Google Home Max.
Among the shortcomings in Consumer Reports’ early tests: The bass was “a bit boomy and overemphasized,” while midrange tones were “hazy” and treble sounds were “underemphasized.” At least the device “played reasonably loudly in a midsized room,” wrote reviewer Allen St. John.
For these reasons, Apple’s AAPL, +3.71% HomePod scored worse in sound quality than the Sonos One and Google Home Max, all of which got “very good” ratings for their audio. The three smart speakers underperformed the publication’s top wireless speakers, however, including the Edifier S1000DB, which costs $350 but it lacks “smart” capabilities. Apple’s HomePod costs $349, while Sonos is selling two Sonos Ones for that price. The Google Home Max goes for $399.
Another negative for the HomePod was its “walled garden” approach, which was flagged by other reviewers as well . Apple’s HomePod only allows users to play Apple Music songs via voice commands, and the device requires an iPhone to set up.
Apple claims that the HomePod senses where it is in a room and adjusts its sound accordingly. “That’s not a feature we evaluated,” St. John wrote.
Apple shares are up 3.8% Monday and 23% over the past 12 months, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +1.58% is up 21%.
